extraction.Name: John Cottier, Senior
extraction.Refused/Protested: he did not want the patent in fee to his 640 acre allotment at the time it was issued, September 29, 1919, but he was told that, if he did not take the patent, it would be taxed just the same, and later sold for same, so he took the patent
extraction.Buyer: sold his whole section to Nels O. Johnson, of Gordon, Nebraska; Johnson paid deponent $2000.00 cash and gave deponent a mortgage for $6000.00 to cover balance due on the transaction; the mortgage was to draw 7 per cent interest and was to run 7 months; to be collected by the First National Bank of Gordon, Nebraska, under Vice President W. E. Brown
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he got behind on taxes on his allotment, and, in 1922, he sold his whole section; Johnson was to pay the taxes
extraction.NOTES: Allotment was 640 acres; mentally incompetent; health is very poor, having been sick for 10 years; wife has poor health and is a cripple; has no one to support but has a son living at home who supports him and his wife; never received any help from the County, State, nor the United States Government; never sold his allotment for any debts incurred prior to receipt of his patent in fee; never heard anything more about the matter and never received any more money on the deal after the letter from W. E. Brown dated October 10, 1923; document sworn March 8, 1929, Shannon County, South Dakota
